arxiv-2102-00697.title: Zero-Error Sum Modulo Two with a Common Observation
arxiv-2102-00697.creator: Milad Sefidgaran, Aslan Tchamkerten
arxiv-2102-00697.description: Abstract This paper investigates the classical modulo two sum problem in source coding, but with a common observation: a transmitter observes ( X , Z ) (X,Z) , the other transmitter observes ( Y , Z ) (Y,Z) , and the receiver wants to compute X ⊕ Y X\oplus Y without error.

arxiv-2111-14472.title: The factorization-assisted topological-amplitude approach and its applications
arxiv-2111-14472.creator: Qin Qin 1 , Chao Wang 2 , Di Wang 3 , Si-Hong Zhou 4
arxiv-2111-14472.description: Abstract Heavy meson decays provide an important platform for studies of both QCD and electroweak dynamics, which may contain some portals to understanding of nonperturbative QCD and physics beyond the Standard Model. The factorization-assisted topological-amplitude approach was proposed to study two-body non-leptonic D D meson decays, where a promising QCD inspired approach from first principles is still missing.

arxiv-2205-04802.title: Vibration-based communication for deafblind people
arxiv-2205-04802.creator: David C. Kutner, Suncica Hadzidedic
arxiv-2205-04802.description: Abstract Deafblind people have both hearing and visual impairments, which makes communication with other people often dependent on expensive technologies e.g., Braille displays, or on caregivers acting as interpreters. This paper presents Morse I/O (MIO), a vibrotactile interface for Android, evaluated through experiments and interviews with deafblind participants.

arxiv-2305-05840.description: Abstract . In the field of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), counterfactual examples explain to a user the predictions of a trained decision model by indicating the modifications to be made to the instance so as to change its associated prediction.

arxiv-2309-07819.title: Decomposition of linear tensor transformations
arxiv-2309-07819.creator: Claudio Turchetti
arxiv-2309-07819.description: Abstract One of the main issues in computing a tensor decomposition is how to choose the number of rank-one components, since there is no finite algorithms for determining the rank of a tensor. A commonly used approach for this purpose is to find a low-dimensional subspace by solving an optimization problem and assuming the number of components is fixed.

arxiv-2309-10349.title: Resolving moving heliospheric structures using interplanetary scintillation observations with the Murchison Widefield Array
arxiv-2309-10349.description: Abstract We have conducted a blind search in 49 consecutive days of interplanetary scintillation observations made by the Murchison Widefield Array from mid-2019, with overlapping daily observations approximately East and South-East of the Sun at an elongation of ∼ \sim 30 degrees and a field of view of 30 degrees. These observations detect an unprecedented density of sources.

arxiv-2311-09753.title: DiffNat: Improving diffusion image quality using natural image statistics
arxiv-2311-09753.creator: Aniket Roy, Maiterya Suin, Anshul Shah, Ketul Shah, Jiang Liu, Rama Chellappa
arxiv-2311-09753.description: Abstract Diffusion models have advanced generative AI significantly in terms of editing and creating naturalistic images. However, efficiently improving generated image quality is still of paramount interest. In this context, we propose a generic “naturalness” preserving loss function, viz., kurtosis concentration (KC) loss, which can be readily applied to any standard diffusion model pipeline to elevate the image quality.

arxiv-2406-14411.title: Performance and scaling analysis of variational quantum simulation
arxiv-2406-14411.creator: Mario Ponce, Thomas Cope, Inés de Vega, Martin Leib
arxiv-2406-14411.description: Abstract We present an empirical analysis of the scaling of the minimal quantum circuit depth required for a variational quantum simulation (VQS) method to obtain a solution to the time evolution of a quantum system within a predefined error tolerance.

arxiv-2408-11256.title: An analogue of Green’s functions for quasiregular maps
arxiv-2408-11256.creator: Mark Broderius, Alastair N. Fletcher
arxiv-2408-11256.description: Abstract . Green’s functions are highly useful in analyzing the dynamical behavior of polynomials in their escaping set. The aim of this paper is to construct an analogue of Green’s functions for planar quasiregular mappings of degree two and constant complex dilatation. These Green’s functions are dynamically natural, in that they semi-conjugate our quasiregular mappings to the real squaring map.

arxiv-2411-08652.title: Accelerating Quasi-Static Time Series Simulations with Foundation Models
arxiv-2411-08652.creator: Alban Puech, François Mirallès, Jonas Weiss, Vincent Mai, Alexandre Blondin Massé, Martin de Montigny, Thomas Brunschwiler, Hendrik F. Hamann
arxiv-2411-08652.description: Abstract Quasi-static time series (QSTS) simulations have great potential for evaluating the grid’s ability to accommodate the large-scale integration of distributed energy resources. However, as grids expand and operate closer to their limits, iterative power flow solvers, central to QSTS simulations, become computationally prohibitive and face increasing convergence issues.

arxiv-2509-05976.title: Reassessing the Spin of Second-born Black Holes in Coalescing Binary Black Holes and Its Connection to the χ eff \chi_{\rm eff} – q q Correlation
arxiv-2509-05976.creator: Zi-Yuan Wang, Ying Qin, Rui-Chong Hu, Yuan-Zhu Wang, Georges Meynet, Han-Feng Song
arxiv-2509-05976.description: Abstract Context. The mass ratio q q and effective inspiral spin χ eff \chi_{\rm eff} of binary black hole mergers in GWTC-4.0 have been reported to display a weaker anti-correlation compared to GWTC-3, a feature whose origin has been explored by several groups.

arxiv-2511-18977.title: FastForward Pruning: Efficient LLM Pruning via Single-Step Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2511-18977.creator: Xin Yuan 1∗ , Siqi Li 1∗ , Jiateng Wei 1 , Chengrui Zhu 1 , Yanming Wu 1 Qingpeng Li 1 , Jiajun Lv 1 , Xiaoke Lan 3 , Jun Chen 2† , Yong Liu 1†
arxiv-2511-18977.description: Abstract Pruning is an effective method for compressing Large Language Models (LLMs), but finding an optimal, non-uniform layer-wise sparsity allocation remains a key challenge. While heuristic methods are fast but yield suboptimal performance, more powerful search-based approaches like Reinforcement Learning (RL) are often hindered by prohibitive computational costs on large-scale models. To overcome this efficiency barrier, we propose FastForward Pruning.

pmc-11674027.title: AMBWO: An Augmented Multi-Strategy Beluga Whale Optimization for Numerical Optimization Problems
pmc-11674027.creator: Guoping You, Zengtong Lu, Zhipeng Qiu, Hao Cheng
pmc-11674027.description: Beluga whale optimization (BWO) is a swarm-based metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the group behavior of beluga whales. BWO suffers from drawbacks such as an insufficient exploration capability and the tendency to fall into local optima. To address these shortcomings, this paper proposes augmented multi-strategy beluga optimization (AMBWO).

pmc-12379983.title: Sleep Duration and Cardiometabolic-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome: The Role of Depressive Symptoms in a Longitudinal Study
pmc-12379983.creator: Yilin Pan, Jingru Bi, Long Feng, Xiaoyun Li
pmc-12379983.description: BackgroundSleep disturbances are increasingly recognized as modifiable risk factors for metabolic and cardiovascular diseases. However, the relationship between sleep duration patterns and Cardiometabolic-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains underexplored, particularly regarding the mediating role of mental health factors. This study investigates the longitudinal association between sleep duration and CKM risk, examining whether depressive symptoms mediate this relationship.

pmc-12618453.title: Discovering dispersion: How robust is automated model discovery for human myocardial tissue?
pmc-12618453.creator: Denisa Martonová, Sigrid Leyendecker, Gerhard A Holzapfel, Ellen Kuhl
pmc-12618453.description: Computational modeling has become an integral tool for understanding the interaction between structural organization and functional behavior in a wide range of biological tissues, including the human myocardium. Traditional constitutive models, and recent models generated by automated model discovery, are often based on the simplifying assumption of perfectly aligned fiber families.

pmc-12712629.title: ﻿Diversity, abundance and distribution of caddisfly (Insecta, Trichoptera) families in relation to environmental parameters across freshwater streams in Singapore
pmc-12712629.creator: Yee Qi Chan, Bryna Jia Ying Liang, Yuchen Ang, John C. Morse, Yixiong Cai, Darren C. J. Yeo
pmc-12712629.description: ﻿AbstractIn land-scarce Singapore, where fresh water is a critical resource, Trichoptera communities can serve as a biomonitoring tool, yet are poorly known. This study seeks to address this gap by establishing a preliminary understanding of trichopteran diversity and distribution in Singapore’s freshwater streams.

pmc-13259095.title: Estimation of Vertical Ground Reaction Forces During Vertical Jumping in Children Using OpenCap
pmc-13259095.creator: Jiongyi You, Zhicheng Lin, Baifa Zhang
pmc-13259095.description: Highlights What are the main findings? OpenCap showed moderate-to-high validity for estimating vertical ground reaction force variables during vertical jumping in young children, with strong agreement for phase durations and mean impulse.The best estimation performance was observed in the propulsive phase, whereas peak force during the landing stabilization phase was substantially underestimated. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13272698.title: Evaluation of modified window-based scatter compensation in quantitative 177Lu-SPECT for a ring-configured CZT SPECT-CT
pmc-13272698.creator: Irma Ceric Andelius, Anna Stenvall, Elias Nilsson, Erik Larsson, Johan Gustafsson
pmc-13272698.description: BackgroundThe aim was to evaluate bias and precision for 177Lu-activity-quantification using window-based scatter compensation in a ring-configured CZT gamma camera (StarGuide™, GE HealthCare). This paper extends a previous study by applying modified scatter compensation (MSC) methods introduced with the StarGuidePlus upgrade. The modified methods account for contamination of scatter windows by primary photons due to tailing.

pmc-13312615.title: Ethnobotanical study of wild edible plants used by the Yao people in Lingyun County, China
pmc-13312615.creator: Xiangtao Cen, Wei Shen, Piyaporn Saensouk, Pathomthat Srisuk, Woranart Thammarong, Surapon Saensouk, Tammanoon Jitpromma
pmc-13312615.description: BackgroundWild edible plants (WEPs) play a vital role in food security, nutrition, and cultural identity among ethnic minority communities in southern China. In the mountainous areas of Guangxi, traditional food systems remain closely connected to local ecosystems. However, quantitative and systematic documentation of WEP diversity and cultural importance among the Yao people is still limited.

pmc-13557795.title: Comparative neuroprotective and antioxidant roles of vitamin E isoforms: a review
pmc-13557795.creator: Liu Yuhong, Koji Fukui
pmc-13557795.description: Vitamin E comprises eight structurally related isoforms, including α-, β-, γ-, and δ-tocopherols and their corresponding tocotrienols. These isoforms differ in the degree of methylation of the chromanol ring and the saturation of the side chain, structural features that critically influence their bioavailability, antioxidant capacity, and neuroprotective functions.

pmc-13670003.title: Clinical Decision Support Models to Optimize Controlled Ovarian Hyperstimulation: A Scoping Review
pmc-13670003.creator: Robin Z. Y. Lu, Toni J. F. Michael, Vinayak Smith, Beverley J. Vollenhoven, Sophie L. Stocker
pmc-13670003.description: Controlled ovarian hyperstimulation (COH) is a precision medicine challenge, with substantial inter‐individual variability in ovarian response affecting treatment efficacy and safety during in vitro fertilization (IVF). Clinical decision support (CDS) tools incorporating statistical, machine learning, and artificial intelligence approaches have been developed to individualize gonadotropin dosing and ovulation trigger timing.
